what_happened: The job to raise [parallel] max_concurrency from 1 to 2 in athena.toml was rejected. The change itself was small, but three athena-cli drain tests (crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, lines 3162, 7706 and 7839) read athena.toml and expect the literal `max_concurrency = 1`. They failed, so the test check failed. The verifier also raised two major findings: CHANGELOG.md was an expected deliverable and was not changed, and the reading did not match the request, so the criteria that passed did not show the request was met. The failed check is the test run, not an acceptance criterion. The event does not list unmet acceptance criteria.
cause: Tests read the live athena.toml and pin its max_concurrency value, so a one-line config edit breaks them. Neither the request nor the reading named those dependent tests, and nothing finds tests that read a config key before the producer edits it. The reading also misstated the request and left out the changelog deliverable, and no check compares the reading with the request or the expected deliverables before the work runs. The only gate that sees all of this is the final verdict, so the job is rejected and not corrected earlier.
prevention: Make the drain tests that need a concurrency of 1 build their own fixture config, so they do not read the live athena.toml. Add a check that fails any test reading a live config key for a pinned value. Before a config-only job is dispatched, also search the tests for references to each key being changed. List those tests in the reading, with permission to fix them or a rule to stop and report, and have the reading include the changelog entry as a deliverable. This removes the whole class of unrelated config edits breaking pinned tests.
proposed_request: Raise [parallel] max_concurrency from 1 to 2 in athena.toml. Outcome: drain can run two jobs at once, and the full test suite passes. First, change the three athena-cli drain tests (crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs near lines 3162, 7706 and 7839) so they build their own config fixture with max_concurrency = 1 and no longer read the value from the live athena.toml. Allowed changes: athena.toml, those tests, and a CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased/Changed saying the default concurrency is now 2. Do not change any production code. Acceptance: (1) athena.toml has max_concurrency = 2; (2) no test reads max_concurrency from the live athena.toml for a pinned value; (3) the full test suite passes; (4) CHANGELOG.md has the entry; (5) the diff touches only the allowed files.
